hero.title: Sree Panayakkal Bhagavathi Temple
hero.sub: അമ്മേ നാരായണ ദേവീ നാരായണ ഭദ്രേ നാരായണ
hero.desc: A sacred abode of Sree Bhagavathi (Bhadrakali), the Grama Devata of Kattikkunnu — fierce toward evil, compassionate toward her devotees, worshipped here in the Kerala Tantric tradition. Near Chembu, Vaikom, this ancient temple blesses devotees through its daily poojas and its grand annual Pooram Mahotsavam.

home.intro: Sree Panayakkal Bhagavathi Temple is the Grama Devata shrine of Kattikkunnu, where Sree Bhagavathi — worshipped as Bhadrakali — has blessed devotees with grace and protection for generations. Regular poojas are held every Tuesday and Friday, on Punartham and Sankramam days, and through other special observances, culminating each year in the grand seven-day Pooram Mahotsavam.

reach.p: Panayakkal Devaswom, Kattikkunnu, Chembu P.O., Vaikom – 686608, Kerala — near Vaikom in Kottayam district. For inquiries: 8086469089 (President), 9446552071 (Secretary).

deity.p: Sree Bhagavathi is worshipped here as Bhadrakali — verily the Mother of the Universe (Jagat Matha), the Parashakti from whom all creation springs. Though she assumed a fierce (Rudra) form to destroy the asura Darika, in her peaceful form she is Lalithambika, granting all wishes to sincere devotees. Devotional tradition describes her as dark as a monsoon cloud, three-eyed, seated upon her vahana Vetalam, bearing sword, shield, and Darika's severed head in her many arms, garlanded with skulls and surrounded by her retinue — all-boon-giving, at once Rudra toward evil and gentle toward her devotees.

verse.devanagari:
काली काली महाकाली भद्रकाली नमोऽस्तुते ।
कुलं च कुलधर्मं च मां च पालय पालय ॥
verse.malayalam:
കാളി കാളി മഹാകാളി ഭദ്രകാളി നമോസ്തുതേ!
കുലം ച കുലധര്‍മ്മം ച മാം ച പാലയ പാലയ!!
verse.transliteration:
Kāli Kāli Mahākāli, Bhadrakāli Namostute!
Kulaṁ cha kuladharmaṁ cha, māṁ cha pālaya pālaya!!
verse.meaning: O Kali, Mahakali, Bhadrakali, I bow to you! Protect my lineage and its dharma, and protect me!

history.p: Sree Panayakkal Bhagavathi Temple is an ancient and sacred shrine at Kattikkunnu, revered as the Grama Devata (village deity) of the locality. Temple rites are led by Tantri Brahmasri Manayathattu Chandrasekharan Namboothiri and Melshanti Brahmasri Kadambanattillam Appukuttan Namboothiri, and the temple is administered by the Panayakkal Devaswom Managing Committee together with several local community organisations (AKDS, KPMS, KSS, NSS and KPSS).

items.name: Sri Ganapathi
items.desc: Remover of obstacles, worshipped first before all undertakings — even the Devas sought his blessing before Palazhi Madhanam.

items.name: Sri Dharmasastha (Ayyappan)
items.desc: A fierce, luminous form honoured especially during the 41-day Mandalapooja each Nov–Dec.

items.name: Durga Devi
items.desc: One of the five goddesses who enable creation; bestows intellect, fame, liberation and happiness on those who take refuge in her.

items.name: Yakshiyamma
items.desc: A protector Desa Devata (regional deity) believed to fulfil the sincere requests of those who seek her refuge.

items.name: Brahmarakshas
items.desc: The protective Brahma-tejas, worshipped as guardian of the temple land and holder of the Guru position.

items.name: Nagarajavu & Nagayakshi
items.desc: Serpent deities worshipped for progeny, wealth and prosperity.

items.name: Pooram Mahotsavam (Mar 3–9)
items.desc: The grand 7-day annual festival featuring the Thiruvabharana procession, Uthram Pongala, nightly Kalamezhuthu Pattu, Darikan & Garudan Thookkam and Mudiyettu, closing with Vadakkupurathu Guruthi before dawn.

items.name: Ezhampooja (Mar 15)
items.desc: After 7 days of closed nada following the Guruthi, the Devi grants darshan again on the closing pooja day, with a special Guruthi Tharppanam within the inner enclosure.

items.name: Navaratri (Oct 18–21)
items.desc: Nine nights honouring the Devi's nine forms, culminating in Durgashtami, Mahanavami and Vijayadashami — with Vidyarambham (children's first-letters ceremony) on Vijayadashami morning.

items.name: Mandalapooja (Nov 17 – Dec 27)
items.desc: A 41-day vratham period honouring Sree Dharmasastha, with daily nada-opening, pooja and vazhipadu through the Makara Vilakku season.

items.name: Vishu & Pathamudayam (Apr 15 & 23)
items.desc: Vishukani is arranged at the sanctum on Vishu morning; Pathamudayam (the 10th day after) is considered especially auspicious for any new undertaking.

items.name: Punartham & Sankramam poojas
items.desc: Every Punartham (birth-star) day and Sankramam (solar transition) day through the year, with Prasada Oottu (community feast) held on Punartham days.

items.name: Kalamezhuthu Pattu
items.desc: On all seven festival evenings, devotees draw the divine form of the Devi on the courtyard mandapam and sing of her deeds. Legend holds that after slaying Darika, the Devi's wrath would not subside — until Shiva blessed the practice, promising that whoever draws her form and sings her praises would be freed of disease and granted prosperity.

items.name: Uthram Pongala
items.desc: A communal rice offering in which devotees light hundreds of hearths together; as the pots boil over, the rice's husk-like "ego" is said to dissolve, symbolically carrying away sin and sorrow with the rising smoke.

items.name: Darikan Thookkam
items.desc: A costumed re-enactment of the arrogant asura Darika challenging every direction to battle, accompanied by Chenda melam and Thalappoli, performed on the final night of the festival.

items.name: Garudan Thookkam
items.desc: Devotees are carried on traditional hanging apparatus depicting Garuda, who — per legend — voluntarily offered his own blood to satisfy the Devi's vahana Vethalam after the battle with Darika.

items.name: Mudiyettu
items.desc: An extremely rare ritual dance-drama, performed only at Bhagavathi shrines, re-enacting the Devi's creation from Shiva's third eye and her destruction of Darika. Offered as a vazhipadu against smallpox, ill omens and adversity.

items.name: Vadakkupurathu Guruthi
items.desc: A symbolic "blood" offering (a turmeric-lime mixture, replacing the animal blood historically offered) made to appease the blood-thirsty Devi after Darika-vadham, marking the ritual close of the festival before dawn.

steps: Outside the Chuttambalam (courtyard), first bow and pray to Yakshiyamma, Brahmarakshas, Nagarajavu and Nagayakshi.
Enter through the eastern nada, praying to the Devi as you step in.
Turn left and pray to Sri Ganapathi, Dharmasastha, and Durga Devi.
Proceed to the front of the Sreekovil and pray to Sree Bhagavathi.
Turn left again, receive theertham and prasadam from the Melshanti, and complete the pradakshinam (circumambulation).
Exit through the northern nada — entry via the southern or western sides is not permitted.

n1.title: Pooram Mahotsavam — March 3–9, 2026
n1.body: The temple's grand annual festival begins with the Thiruvabharana Ghoshayathra on March 3 and continues through Uthram Pongala, Kalamezhuthu Pattu, and Darikan & Garudan Thookkam, and Mudiyettu, concluding with Vadakkupurathu Guruthi before dawn on March 9. All devotees are cordially invited.

n2.title: Book Prasada Oottu & Mudiyettu in Advance
n2.body: Prasada Oottu (held on all Punartham and festival days) and 2027 Mudiyettu slots are now open for booking. Mudiyettu sponsorship ₹12,000 (advance ₹2,000); Darikan Thookkam ₹1,300; Garudan Thookkam ₹2,100. Call 8086469089 / 9446552071 to reserve.

n3.title: Temple Darshan Order
n3.body: Please enter through the eastern nada, pray to Yakshiyamma, Brahmarakshas and the Naga deities first, then turn left past Sri Ganapathi, Dharmasastha and Durga Devi to reach the Sreekovil. Complete the pradakshinam and exit through the northern nada; entry via the southern or western sides is not permitted.

n4.title: Ezhampooja — March 15, 2026
n4.body: After 7 days of closed nada following Vadakkupurathu Guruthi, the Devi grants Ezhampooja darshan on March 15 (Meenam 1, Thiruvonam) — extra auspicious this year as it coincides with Ekadasi. Includes Akamkalathil Ezhaam Guruthi Tharppanam at 10 AM and Prasada Oottu at 12:30 PM.
